title: Longest ZigZag Path in a Binary Tree
summary: Given a binary tree, find the longest path where each step alternates between moving left and right.
statement: Given a binary tree, find the longest path where each step alternates between moving left and right. The path length is defined as the number of transitions minus one, with a single node having a length of zero.
constraints: A ZigZag path alternates left and right child edges and may start at any node.
Return its length in edges, so a one-node path has length zero.

reference_solution:
def longest_tree_zigzag(root):
    answer=0
    def visit(node,left_length,right_length):
        nonlocal answer
        if node is None:return
        answer=max(answer,left_length,right_length)
        visit(node.left,right_length+1,0);visit(node.right,0,left_length+1)
    visit(root,0,0);return answer

hints: At each node, track the current path length whose latest edge came from each direction.
Moving left extends the prior right-ending path and resets the left-ending alternative; moving right is symmetric.
Update a global maximum, then recurse with the two transformed lengths.
Every start is represented by a reset-to-zero state, while every alternating continuation extends the opposite direction only.
editorial: Depth-first traversal carries the best alternating length ending at each node from each incoming direction. A left edge extends a right-ending path and resets the other state, and vice versa. Taking a maximum at every node covers all starts. The oracle independently walks a forced alternating direction from every node.
